h: Torah and Prayer Remain the Strength of Israel

p: "And Tziyon said: Hashem has forsaken me,
and my Lord has forgotten me" (Yeshayahu 49:14).
Tziyon is the name of the place of the Mikdash,
and there is the place of the Torah,
"For from Tziyon will go forth Torah,
and the word of Hashem from Yerushalayim."
And there is the shining forth
of the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh,
"If a matter is too wondrous for you," etc.,
"then you shall rise and go up," etc.
And the Torah is called the Name of Hashem,
"From where is the blessing over the Torah
'When I call the Name of Hashem,
And in the holy Zohar it is found
is the Name of HaKadosh Baruch Hu.
So too the Beis HaMikdash is called
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
and as Shlomo HaMelech, alav hashalom, said
that one who prays must direct himself
"And they pray toward this house," etc.;
the hill toward which all mouths turn."
And in prayer one says at the start (Tehillim 51:17):
for prayer is in the secret of a servant,
to the hand of their masters."
And this is the whole strength of Yisrael,
that their strength is only in their mouth,
and this is the voice of Torah and the voice of prayer.
And this is "And Tziyon said: Hashem has forsaken me":
and this corresponds to the voice of Torah;
corresponds to the voice of prayer.
are only from the power of Hashem Yisbarach:
sends the prayer into a person's mouth,
so that it be "the mouth of Hashem";
in the name of our master the Rebbe Reb Elimelech,
עַל אִם שְׁגוּרָה תְּפִלָּתִי בְּפִי (בְּרָכוֹת ה, ה)
on "If my prayer is fluent in my mouth" (Mishnah Berachos 5:5):
that it is sent by Hashem Yisbarach
And regarding Torah too we find,
בְּכָל מָקוֹם אֲשֶׁר אַזְכִּיר אֶת שְׁמִי
"In every place where I cause My Name to be mentioned";
regarding one who sits and occupies himself with Torah
that the Shechinah is with him;
which is called the Name of Hashem,
and it is written "I cause My Name to be mentioned,"
shines the words of Torah into his heart.
"Hashem has forsaken me, and my Lord has forgotten me,"
in the seven haftaros of consolation
שֶׁעָבְרוּ יוֹתֵר מִן י״ח מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה
that more than eighteen hundred years have passed
and we have not yet been saved.
"Can a woman forget her nursing child?";
for this answers what was said,
which is the aspect of fear,
And it alludes to the voice of prayer,
"They will fear You with the sun,"
כָּל הָרָגִיל לָבוֹא לְבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת וְכוּלֵּי
"Whoever regularly comes to the synagogue," etc.,
וְכֵן נִדְרַשׁ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג קצו, א)
And it is the middah of Malchus,
"A king, that his fear be upon you."
And the Shechinah is called Mother,
the sound of his mother's footsteps,
I will rise before the Shechinah that is coming."
come from the union of Abba and Imma.
And that is why it says,
"Can a woman forget her nursing child?":
for it is impossible that there be in this
וְאַחַר כָּךְ מְסַיֵּים הַהַפְטוֹרָה (שָׁם נא, ג)
"Joy and gladness will be found in her":
that it refers to Torah she'b'al peh
"And I will gladden them in My house of prayer";
in the name of our master the Rebbe Reb Elimelech,
that the sign for a person
that his prayer has been accepted
is that joy comes into his heart,
for Shabbos corresponds to the seventh middah,
we call it Torah she'b'al peh."
And as for prayer, it is found (Shabbos 118b):
is granted the requests of his heart," etc.;
along the lines of what it says (Yeshayahu 65:24):
"And it will be that before they call,
רַק רְצוֹן יְרֵאָיו יַעֲשֶׂה (תְּהִלִּים קמה, יט)
only "He does the will of those who fear Him" (Tehillim 145:19).
